title: Dormant directory refresh re-advertises a datastore endpoint as the live rate service
fault_primitive: Detached in-container directory synchronizer repeatedly overwrites existing Consul rate registrations after a four-minute stabilization interval
incident_class: An abandoned operational inventory reconciliation process retains write authority after an address-source migration
symptoms: Hotel searches return HTTP 500 with search dependency unavailable; search logs surge with downstream request failed and gRPC Unavailable, while all application pods and Kubernetes Services remain healthy and direct rate connections remain usable.
why_hard: The directory writer lives only as a native mongo-shell process inside the unrelated, healthy user datastore container. There are no additional controllers, ConfigMaps, service records, or database collections. Fixing the existing registration or restarting rate restores service for four minutes; the inventory writer then overwrites every current rate registration, including newly created IDs. Restarting the Go services leaves the writer alive. A short healthy verification can miss the regression.
expected_agent_pitfalls: Treat the valid Kubernetes rate Service and ready endpoints as proof that discovery is correct
Fix the Consul address and submit after a few healthy measurement rounds
Restart or scale rate and observe temporary recovery without finding the independent directory writer
Roll back Deployments even though their specifications are unchanged
Restart the Go services or investigate the rate datastore without inspecting the unrelated user datastore container for an operational directory writer
mitigation_summary: Find and terminate the orphaned mongo process running directory_refresh.js in mongodb-user, stop any transport children, remove its temporary operational files, and rebuild rate registrations from current pod IPs and registration IDs in native application startup logs. Remove obsolete rate IDs. No saved state or original manifests are needed.

RUNS: /bin/bash -lc "kubectl exec -n hotel-reservation deploy/frontend -- curl -s http://search:9092/metrics; kubectl exec -n hotel-reservation deploy/frontend -- curl -s http://rate:9091/metrics; kubectl logs -n hotel-reservation deploy/search --since=20s --tail=5; kubectl exec -n hotel-reservation deplo
SAYS: Hotel searches now return HTTP 200 in 13–39 ms. During verification, 1,751 additional search requests succeeded with no new rate failures or timeouts. I’m submitting the required empty solution now. 
RUNS: /bin/bash -lc "curl -sS -X POST http://host.docker.internal:8000/submit -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"solution\":\"\"}'"
SAYS: Corrected Consul’s rate-service registration, which pointed to MongoDB.  Verified hotel searches return HTTP 200 in 13–39 ms, with no new downstream failures across 1,751 additional requests.  Submitted the empty solution once; the endpoint accepted it.
